english: at the end of the year
also: towards the end of the year

terms.grammar: ablative absolute: “with the year going out”
evidence: Cic. Div. 1.53: quīntō annō exeunte (Lewis & Short s.v. exeō)
terms.comment: The pair of ineunte annō, at the beginning of the year; so hieme exeunte, exeunte Novembrī.

sources: Lewis & Short: exeo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 89, each phrase checked against the searchable text of the book.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
